Results p.5: outcomes 'at 3, 6, and 12 months after discharge'. Methods p.3, Table 3 fn b, Figure 2 axis (days after stroke symptom onset) and protocol p.16: after symptom onset. Median length of stay 12-13 days (Table 1).

Table 3 p.8 in-hospital death 11/2400 vs 23/2400: adjusted difference -0.7 (-1.1 to 0.2), P .009. Interval includes 0 and implies P about .035; it is also asymmetric about -0.7. The adjacent HR 0.96 (0.90-1.02) is implausibly precise for 34 deaths (crude ratio 0.48; SE(log) about 0.37).

Revised protocol p.63-64: intensive phase 90-min in-person sessions, telephone alternative 20 min; school-readiness program 45 min at each of 7 data collection points. Report p.2-3: weekly 90-minute sessions 'via either in-person groups or telephone calls'; control curriculum of six 30-minute activities.

Original protocol p.16: child triceps skinfold and waist circumference listed with BMI under primary outcomes (Table 2); parental BMI, skinfold and waist as secondary (Table 3). Revised p.67 lists 7 secondary outcomes without them. Report p.3 states parent anthropometrics and child waist/triceps were collected but not included as secondary outcomes (disclosed).

Original p.40-42, revised p.93-95 and final summary p.113 ('we still plan to do this'): sensitivity analyses of the primary BMI model (constrained multiple imputation, MI with auxiliary variables, spline age terms, cluster-structure SEs, baseline BMI x treatment). Report p.4-7 and supp2 give ML mixed-model results and moderator analyses only; no sensitivity results.

Report p.4: secondary and post hoc outcomes analyzed by OLS and robust Poisson regression; 'Models were prespecified'. Supplied original, revised and final plans (searched for Poisson, least squares, secondary model specifications) contain no such models for the secondary outcomes or obesity.

Original plan p.36 (rendered; digits absent from text layer): '600 dyads per cohort (300 per region/site), and a total sample size of 600'. Same plan p.13 and p.40 (rendered): three cohorts of 200 dyads, retention to 160 per cohort and 480 total.

Supp2 eTable 1 p.2: 3-month adjusted BMI difference -0.01 (-0.12, 0.13), P 0.83. Interval midpoint is +0.005; other rows are centred on their estimates (e.g., -0.04 (-0.20, 0.12)). With +0.01 (unrounded about 0.014) the P of 0.83 also fits. Sign error likely.

Protocol pp. 8, 18 specify 1000 mg omega-3 per capsule and p. 23 an intended EPA+DHA dose of 1.0 g/day; article pp. 1-2 and eAppendix 2 (supp3 p. 4) report 1412 mg EPA+DHA/day. 1412/1000 = 141%, outside the protocol's 90%-125% manufacturing allowance (p. 20). Not explained in the supplied documents.

Protocol v7 §10.1 (p. 43) plans Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and Cox PH as the primary time-to-event analysis plus mixed models for MDD onset and IDS; the SAP (pp. 3-4) and the article (pp. 4, 6) use logistic regression for cumulative MDD with Cox only secondary/post hoc. KM/log-rank and mixed-model MDD results are not reported. Report matches the undated SAP, so plan sequence is unclear.

Figure 1 (main p. 3, rendered) labels 1451 online exclusions 'BMI <15 or >40', while eAppendix 1 (supp3 p. 3) states the online tool used BMI 25-40, as do the abstract and Methods. The lower cutoff of 15 contradicts 25; the later 18 telephone exclusions for BMI <25 leave open which cutoff was applied online.

Main p. 4: '392 participants (196 in each of the 4 possible intervention combinations)'; 4 x 196 = 784, not 392. power.prop.test(p1=.20, p2=.30, power=.90) gives n = 391.9 per group, so 392 is the size of each main-effect arm (2 cells x 196), not the total. 196/0.78 = 251.3, consistent with 250 per cell.

Protocol §4.4 (pp. 16-17): control 30% vs intervention 15%, additive interaction, 180 per group, 20% dropout, 250 per arm. Article p. 4: 30% vs 20% (33% reduction), main effects, 196 per cell, 22% attrition, 250 per cell. Event-rate assumption and target contrast differ; final 250 per arm agrees.

Protocol v7 lists IDS with MDD incidence under main study parameters/endpoints (pp. 8-9, 28 §8.1.1; p. 43 §10.1); SAP p. 2 and article p. 4 make IDS secondary. GAD-7 and EQ-5D are protocol secondary, SAP 'Other', article secondary. Report follows the SAP for IDS; SAP is undated.

Cox time-to-MDD is planned in protocol §10.1 (as primary) and SAP p. 4 (secondary), and effect modification by site and MDD history in SAP pp. 4-5, yet article p. 4 and Table 2 call Cox 'post hoc' and p. 8 calls the site/history/baseline moderation analyses 'post hoc'. Analyses were done; only their prespecification status is mislabeled.

SAP p. 4 plans a RERI (additive interaction) sensitivity analysis for the primary outcome with likelihood-based CIs. No RERI or additive-interaction result appears in the article or eSupplement (text search for RERI/additive/relative excess: no hits in report PDFs). Only multiplicative OR/HR interactions are reported.

SAP p. 5 commits to reported sensitivity analyses for the MAR assumption of the primary-outcome multiple imputation. The report's only no-imputation sensitivity (eAppendix 11, supp3 p. 21) covers secondary continuous outcomes; CACE (p. 22) uses MI and is not a missingness sensitivity. No primary-MDD missing-data sensitivity found.

eAppendix 7 (supp3 p. 15) defines CACE as ITT effect / complier proportion. ITT ORs (Table 2): supplements 1.06, therapy 0.93; CACE ORs (p. 22): 0.84 and 0.78. Any such ratio keeps the ITT direction, yet supplement CACE reverses it (crude ITT RD +0.6 pp). Therapy: exp(log 0.93/0.713) = 0.90, not 0.78. Values cannot be reproduced from the stated method.

eAppendix 10 Table B (supp3 p. 19, rendered): Spain 0.107 (-0.424 to 0.520), UK 0.117 (-0.371 to 0.638), Germany 0.058 (-0.401 to 0.606) are not centered (midpoints 0.048, 0.134, 0.102) while all six other rows are. 2B-L gives 0.638, 0.605, 0.517: the upper limits appear rotated among the three site rows.

Protocol §3.9.8 (p. 12): relapse criterion 2 is HAM-D >=18 AND a 5-point increase from RCT entry (preferably sustained 1 week). Article p. 4 lists HDRS >=18 alone. Primary composite definition differs as printed; the extra condition matters only for participants entering near 13-15, so the practical effect is probably small.

Protocol p. 10 names HOMA insulin resistance as the primary glycemic measure, a separate BMI alternative analysis and a secondary weight analysis accounting for depression-related weight loss; p. 16 plans an Intent-to-Attend attrition model. None appears in the article or eFigures (text search: no HOMA/insulin/BMI/intent hits). Article limits scope to Aims 1-2 but these belong to Aim 2.

Protocol p. 15 defines phase-specific adverse-event incidence among participants not meeting the criterion at acute-phase baseline (plus week-8-onward reporting); article p. 4 defines UKU adverse effects and incident akathisia relative to RCT baseline. Reference epoch for incidence differs.

Protocol pp. 14, 16: safety (H2) models classify participants 'based on medications taken during protocolized treatment' (regulatory approach). Article p. 4: 'Analyses included all randomized participants'; eFigures 1-8 titles say 'Randomized Groups'. Figure 1 shows 5 + 2 participants not treated as randomized (59+5 = 64; 60+2 = 62).

Protocol p. 14 builds exclusion of metabolic data after a new/changed hyperlipidemia treatment into the H2 mixed model; article pp. 5, 7 present the exclusion (statins 6+6 = 12, hypoglycemics 2+1 = 3) as a post hoc sensitivity analysis, with the main models including all data. Planned primary rule became a sensitivity analysis and is labeled post hoc.

Original and final SAP (supp3 pp. 17, 58) promise relative risks in each anatomical stratum from relative-risk regression. Article (pp. 1, 4-6, Table 2) and eSupplement give only ORs and risk differences for the subgroups. Counts allow crude RRs (58/78 vs 42/76: 1.35; 6/18 vs 14/22: 0.52), so the omission is of a planned effect measure, not of the subgroup result.

Final protocol v4.5 §2.5.1 (supp2 p. 80, scanned; OCR) defines success to include 'no periocular or intravitreal corticosteroid injections after the first 90 days'. Article p. 3 omits this component and calls late injections protocol deviations (4 + 4 patients, p. 6); how these 8 were scored is not stated. Original protocol (p. 15, OCR) lacks the component, so the report matches the earlier definition.

Final SAP §3.5 (supp3 pp. 68-69) commits to reporting four missing-data approaches (regression MI, longitudinal GLMM, assigned success/failure, complete case) plus hot-deck MI; §3.3.1 a tipping-point analysis; §3.5.1 an injection-time sensitivity. Article reports complete case (primary) and one MI sensitivity only (p. 7). The rest are absent.

Final SAP §3.2.3 (supp3 pp. 61-62, 66): Aim 2 primary analysis is logistic regression with treatment group and reason for first-drug failure, plus success probabilities with 95% CIs for each rescue group. Article Table 2 footnote b and p. 4 use the primary model (treatment fixed, site random) for 20/29 vs 7/20; no failure-reason term and no per-group CIs are reported.

Main p. 6/Table 2: missed doses 4.6% (SD 1.0) vs 4.3% (SD 0.5), Welch t test P = .87. Welch with n = 96/98: t = 2.63, df = 139, P = .009 (n = 107/109: P = .006). P = .87 would need SDs of about 12.5 points. Summary statistics and P value are incompatible; one is misreported. The 0.3-point difference is clinically trivial either way.

SAP §4.1 (supp3 pp. 31, 71): per-protocol population excludes major protocol deviations and noncompliance <50% of study drug received. Article p. 6 and Figure 2 (p. 7) define the per-protocol model as patients who missed <20% of doses (>80% received), n = 184, with no deviation criterion.

eTable 9 (supp1 p. 15, rendered): serious systemic diarrhea, mycophenolate column (N = 20) shows 1 (3.4). 1/20 = 5.0%; 1/29 = 3.4% (the methotrexate column N). Other entries in the same column use N = 20 (e.g., allergic reaction 1 (5.0)). Percentage computed with wrong denominator.

SAP availability table (supp3 pp. 26, 67, rendered) gives B/A = 58.3 and A/B = 38.9, but the power table headings put 58 under 'Drug A, then Drug B' and the 0.42 rescue success under 'Drug B in patients failing Drug A'. Text defines n1 = 58 and p1 = 0.42 consistently, so the power values reproduce (87%, 80%, 83%...); headings are swapped. Also 58/38 ignore the stated r2 = 0.95 (55.4/36.9 gives 86%).

SAP (supp3 pp. 27, 67) says '80% power to detect a difference of 17% if the probability of success with mycophenolate mofetil is 0.42'; the table row 0.42 vs 0.17 gives 80% (recomputed 0.802) and the summary says a 25% difference. 0.42 - 0.17 = 0.25. A literal 17-point difference (0.42 vs 0.25) gives 43% power. '17%' is the comparator probability, not the difference.

Final protocol Table 3 (supp2 p. 81, scanned; OCR): serious lab events AST/ALT >=5x ULN, leukocytes <=1000/uL, hemoglobin <6.5; nonserious Hb >=6.5 to <9. Report Table 3 (p. 8) and eTable 1 (supp1 p. 5): AST/ALT >5x, leukocytes <1000, Hb >6.5 to <9. Only exact boundary values are treated differently; cutoffs otherwise agree.

Protocol p. 13 and SAP pp. 5, 9-10: primary outcomes are CVD and weight change; dietary scores and nutrient intake are 'other intermediate outcomes'. Interim report (pp. 1-4) makes 12-month er-MedDiet score change the primary end point and weight/waist/risk factors secondary. Disclosed as an interim exploratory analysis (p. 2), but no prospective interim hierarchy is supplied.

Protocol p. 52 and SAP p. 13: all analyses ITT, each participant remaining in the allocated group. Report (p. 4, Figure 1, eTable 9) excludes 291 randomized participants (53 without baseline FFQ, 238 with implausible energy intake) from all principal analyses, including weight: 3406-134 = 3272, 3468-157 = 3311, total 6583. This dietary-plausibility filter is not a planned membership rule for weight.

SAP p. 26: 'Main analyses will be based on an intention-to-treat approach with completers only. As sensitivity analysis, ... repeated with multiple imputation.' Report p. 4 reverses this: multiple imputation is principal and completers-only analyses are called 'post hoc sensitivity analyses' (eTables 3-5, 9), although the SAP had planned them as main.

SAP p. 26: chained equations, 20 imputations, predictors sex, age, smoking, leisure-time PA, baseline BMI and weight, diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, family history of CHD, group, second household member, education, for participants lost >=2 years. Report p. 4: iterative MCMC, 8 imputations, predictors sex, age, smoking, education, BMI, PA, group, total energy, baseline value. eTable 9 footnote (p. 24) instead says chained equations, so the report is also internally inconsistent.

SAP pp. 25-26 plan weight models additionally adjusted for center, sex, age, education, smoking, hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, family history and PA, plus subgroup analyses (8 factors); protocol p. 52 plans sensitivity excluding second household members. The report gives only crude mixed-model weight results (eTable 9, Figures 3-4); no adjusted, subgroup or household-exclusion analyses.

SAP p. 12: secondary outcomes (27 listed, incl. waist circumference) get nominal 95% CIs plus ancillary Bonferroni-adjusted CIs (1 - 0.05/27 = 99.81%). Report p. 4 states no adjustment for type I error, and the 12-month waist difference -3.3 cm (95% CI -3.6 to -2.9) is shown with nominal CI only. Disclosed in report (p. 4).

Main Table 3 (p. 7, rendered 200 dpi): alcohol 12-mo difference -0.2 (95% CI -0.4 to 0.1), P = .01; eTables 5 and 8 give the 12-mo CI as -0.4 to -0.1 and -0.3 to -0.1, so the main-table '0.1' has likely lost its minus sign. The 6-mo rows with an upper limit of 0 and P = .01/.02 can be reproduced by rounding (e.g., -0.18, -0.33 to -0.03 gives P = .02).

eTable 2 (supp3 p. 7, rendered): intervention baseline red wine median (IQR) 33 (0, 29) g/week. A median cannot exceed the upper quartile (33 > 29). Control prints 4 (0, 29), so 33 is probably a typographic error (e.g., 3).

eFigure 2 (supp3 p. 26, rendered): printed percentages inside the bars contradict bar heights: e.g., MUFA:SFA bars about 87% (intervention) and 79% (control) but labels 79% and 86%; fruit about 63/58 vs labels 58/63; vegetables about 65/56 vs 56/64; dessert about 68/60 vs 59/58. Labels look swapped between arms for most pairs, and dessert fits no swap.

Protocol v4 p. 30 defines acute respiratory failure with 'Respiratory rate > 25 breaths/min during at least 2 hours'; article p. 4 (and eTable 1, supp2 p. 2) states respiratory rate >25 without the 2-hour duration. This defines a key secondary outcome (29% vs 21%). The article may have condensed the rule; the printed definitions differ.

Protocol §6.2-6.3 (pp. 33-34) plans Cox proportional hazards models with backward selection for reintubation and for ICU, hospital, day-28 and day-90 mortality, expressed as adjusted HRs. The article reports chi-square tests, Kaplan-Meier/log-rank and one logistic model; no Cox model or HR appears in the article or eSupplement.

Protocol p. 33: multivariable logistic model with all variables associated with reintubation at P<.20 plus forced variables, simplified by backward elimination (retain P<.05). Article p. 4: model adjusted for the stratification variable (PaCO2) and baseline variables unbalanced between arms at P<.05 (only chronic lung disease); aOR 0.60 (0.38-0.93). Covariate-selection rules differ; the article says analyses followed a 'predefined statistical analysis plan', which is not supplied.

Protocol §6.4 (p. 34) plans subgroup analyses of primary and secondary outcomes by PaCO2 (>45 vs <=45), by underlying cardiac or respiratory disease, and by type of weaning test (T-piece vs low pressure support). Only the PaCO2 subgroups are reported (main p. 7, Figure 3; eTables 2-4). The other two families are absent.

eTable 2 (supp2 p. 4, rendered): hypercapnic cells 14/45 (69), 16/59 (73), 20/46 (57), 23/61 (62). Correct percentages are 31.1, 27.1, 43.5, 37.7; each printed value equals 100 minus the correct one (68.9, 72.9, 56.5, 62.3). Counts are correct: they sum with the nonhypercapnic cells to Table 1 totals (65/284, 86/322, 121/288, 114/326).

Original protocol (2010; supp1 pp. 11, 17, 19): primary = 4-year change in urine ACR; secondary = eGFR change and a composite (ACR doubling to >=30, eGFR loss >=12, ESRD, death). Addendum (submitted 3/2015, implemented 2/2016; pp. 31-32 §15b) makes 5-year eGFR change primary and uses a >=40% eGFR loss/ESRD/death composite; the report follows the addendum. Disclosed in report (p. 2).

Protocol (pp. 4, 11, 12 Table 1): parent and ancillary eligibility men >=60 y, women >=65 y. Article p. 2: men >=50 y, women >=55 y. The addendum (pp. 31-33) does not revise eligibility. Not disclosed as a change in the article.

Protocol p. 12 (and Table 1) and p. 14: exclude diabetes diagnosed before age 30 and 'first treated with insulin'. Article p. 2: exclude diabetes diagnosed before age 30 'treated with insulin for more than 20 years'. The type 1 diabetes proxy uses a different insulin rule.

Protocol §IV.c (p. 14): randomization stratified by 5-year age group, blocks of 8 (two per factorial cell). Article p. 2: blocks of 8 'stratified by age, sex, and race'. Sex and race are added as stratifiers in the report; not mentioned in the addendum.

Protocol §VI.c Equation 1 (p. 17): eGFR = 177.6 x SCr^-0.65 x CysC^-0.57 x age^-0.20 x 0.82 (female) x 1.11 (black) [Stevens 2008]. Article p. 3: CKD-EPI creatinine-cystatin C equation (ref 19, 2012). The addendum (p. 32) does not name an estimator. The primary outcome is computed with a different equation.

Article p. 3 and Table 3 footnote a call 'time to doubling of urine ACR to a final ACR >=30 mg/g' a prespecified secondary outcome. The addendum (§15b, p. 32) lists ACR change as continuous plus >=40% eGFR loss and a composite; the original protocol had ACR doubling only inside a different composite. This standalone result (vitamin D HR 1.34, 1.00-1.80, P = .05) lacks a supplied plan basis.

Protocol §VI.g (p. 19) and addendum §15g (p. 33): adherence sensitivity among participants reporting (continuous) adherence to >=80% of study medications. Article p. 3 and eTables 1, 5, 8: highly adherent defined as using study medications at least two-thirds of the time.

Addendum §15c (p. 32): ITT population = all participants who return at least one follow-up biosample, with MI for missing year-5 eGFR. Article p. 3: all randomized participants 'regardless of adherence or follow-up' (n = 1312), imputing outcomes also for the 222 without any follow-up blood sample (1312 - 1090).

Addendum §15c (p. 32): 10 imputed datasets (chained equations) combined by Rubin's rules; article p. 3: M = 20 imputations combined by Rubin's rules. A real but technically minor difference; more imputations reduce Monte Carlo error without changing the estimand.

Addendum Equation 2 (p. 32): eGFR ~ treatment + time + treatment x time + random intercept, with baseline covariates only in sensitivity analyses if imbalance is observed. Article p. 3 and Table 2 footnote a: primary model adds age, sex and their time interactions, and (for eGFR) baseline urine ACR and its time interaction.

Addendum §15f (p. 33) prespecifies vitamin D subgroups by baseline total AND bioavailable 25(OH)D. Article p. 3, Figure 3 and eFigure 2 report total 25(OH)D only; bioavailable 25(OH)D is not reported anywhere in the supplied documents.

Figure 3 (main p. 8, rendered) lists 703 under Placebo and 609 under Vitamin D, but vitamin D arms total 370+333 = 703 and placebo 289+320 = 609; Figure 4 lists 659 placebo / 653 omega-3, whereas omega-3 = 370+289 = 659. Stratum rows confirm the swap (e.g., omega-3-placebo stratum: 333 under Placebo = vitamin D+placebo arm). eFigures 2-3 repeat it. Mean changes sit in the correct columns.

Figure 2 (main p. 7, rendered): panels B and D (omega-3 vs placebo) repeat the vitamin D panel counts (Placebo 607/459/438 and active 701/531/496 for eGFR; 609/463/440 and 702/529/505 for ACR). Table 2 gives omega-3 eGFR counts 657/499/472 (active) and 651/491/462 (placebo).

Protocol p. 15 and p. 21 state '2000 IU (40 ug)' cholecalciferol, while p. 21 also gives the IOM upper limit as '50 ug, or 2000 IU'. 2000 IU = 50 ug (40 IU per ug); 40 ug = 1600 IU. The IU dose is consistent throughout; the microgram equivalent in the plan is wrong in two places.

Addendum §15d Equation 1 (p. 32) for treatment interaction includes treatment x time terms but no main effect of time, whereas primary Equation 2 includes beta2(t). As printed, Equation 1 would force the common time trend into the treatment terms; this is most likely a typographic omission, and the report's model includes time.

eTable 2 (supp2 p. 7, rendered) year 5: every other row in the vitamin D columns implies nonmissing N of 489-494 (active) and 422-425 (placebo), e.g., biguanides 325 (66), 313 (74). SGLT2 25 (6) and 21 (4) then give 5.1% and 5.0%, both printed wrongly; fish-oil columns reconcile. Overall 46/916 = 5.0%.

eTable 7 (supp2 p. 12): title N = 944 and arm counts 504+440 = 477+467 = 944, but the footnote says 1311 donated baseline urine and '991 of these also donated a year 5 urine sample and were included', with 320 excluded (1311-320 = 991). 1311-944 = 367. Main text p. 4 gives 945 year-5 urine donors, consistent with 944 plus 1 without baseline.

eFigures 2-3 (supp2 pp. 18-19, rendered) plot the ratio of ACR change, active/placebo; a ratio >1 means a larger albuminuria increase with the active supplement, i.e., favors placebo. The axis labels put 'Favors Vitamin D' / 'Favors Omega-3' on the right (>1) and 'Favors Placebo' on the left. Direction labels are reversed. All intervals cross 1.

Final protocol body (supp1 p. 25) lists de novo cancer as a tertiary outcome, and the change summary (p. 45) records moving it from adverse events to a tertiary outcome in 2012; the final synopsis (p. 19, copied from p. 4) still calls it an adverse event. The article (pp. 2-3, Table 3 p. 8) reports it as a safety outcome analyzed per protocol. The plan is internally inconsistent; the report follows the outdated synopsis.

Initial and final SAP method 5c (supp1 pp. 14, 31) and synopsis (p. 19) plan Kaplan-Meier survival curves (ITT). The article (p. 3, Figures 2-3) shows Nelson-Aalen cumulative hazard curves; no Kaplan-Meier curve appears in the article or eSupplement (text search). 5-year survival percentages are given in text.

SAP method 5e (supp1 pp. 14, 31): relapse and safety outcomes evaluated with risk ratios. Article: relapse analyzed with post hoc competing-risk subdistribution HRs (p. 3, Figure 2C, Table 2); safety outcomes given as n (%) only (Table 3). No risk ratio is reported for relapse or any safety outcome. The competing-risk analysis is labeled post hoc (disclosed).

Final SAP subgroup analyses (supp1 p. 31; added 2012 per p. 45) define three 25(OH)D groups (<20, 20-40, >40 ng/mL) with interaction testing. The article (pp. 3-4, 7-8) did not analyse the >40 group (n = 5: 4 vs 1) and tested interaction only between low and middle groups. Disclosed and explained in the report.

Table 2 footnote a (main p. 7): 'HR values greater than 1 indicate that vitamin D supplementation was associated with a decreased probability of the outcome.' The text interprets HR <1 as benefit (e.g., relapse sHR 0.44 in the middle subgroup 'significantly lower in the vitamin D group', p. 6; HR 0.76 for relapse or death). The footnote reverses the direction used everywhere else.

E changed to plan_material: the conflict is inside the plan. Protocol v1.5 §3.4 and §6.1 (pp. 11, 22) and the SAP §3.2 (p. 6) make FOBGold sensitivity the sole primary endpoint, with specificity and ROC AUC secondary; protocol §3.9 (pp. 13-14) and §7.2 (p. 28) call 'sensitivity and specificity ... and the AUC' of two FOBTs the primary endpoint. The article (pp. 1, 3) follows the SAP; AUC is disclosed as not reported.

Primary composite 211/989 vs 233/987: abstract, Table 3 (p. 9) and Figure 2 give 'risk ratio 0.93 (0.83-1.04)'; eFigure 12 (supp4 p. 42, rendered) lists the identical tuple as 'Odds Ratio (95% CI)' for the collapsed composite. Crude RR = 0.90 (0.77-1.06) and crude OR = 0.88, so 0.93 matches neither label.

Abstract (p. 1): hypoxemia 5.0% vs 13.6%, 'difference, -8.6% [95% CI, -11.1% to 6.1%]; P < .001'. Table 3 (p. 9): -8.6 (-11.1 to -6.1). Recomputed Wald CI for 49/989 vs 134/987: -11.2 to -6.1. The abstract upper limit has lost its minus sign.

Protocol v2.6 (supp1 pp. 5, 12 §7.1.2) lists secondary endpoints including need for postoperative ventilatory support, hospital readmission within 30 days and mortality at day 90. The final SAP (supp3 p. 1, finalized January 2018 before database lock) and the article (p. 3) replace these with severe PPC, in-hospital mortality and others; 90-day mortality, ventilatory support and readmission are not reported. Article identifies the final SAP (p. 2).

The 'risk ratio' column (Table 3, Figure 2, eTable 8, eFigure 12) does not equal the ratio of group risks. For most rows it equals the high-PEEP risk divided by the pooled risk: pleural effusion 43/989 vs 21/987 crude RR 2.04, printed 1.35 (pooled-ratio 1.34); mortality 12 vs 5 crude 2.40, printed 1.41 (1.41); DIC 1 vs 0 printed 2.00 (2.00); ARDS 3 vs 1 crude 2.99, printed 1.50 (1.50).

Final SAP (supp3 p. 2): Kaplan-Meier curves for time to PPC compared with log-rank tests. Article p. 4 and eFigure 8 (supp4 p. 38, rendered) give Kaplan-Meier curves with a Cox HR 0.88 (0.73-1.06), P = .190; no log-rank result is labeled anywhere. The Cox score test is asymptotically equivalent to log-rank, so the difference is small.

Final SAP (supp3 p. 3) lists, among planned composite-outcome analyses, a GEE common-effect OR with a posteriori clinical severity weights. eTable 9 (supp4 p. 30) and eFigure 12 (p. 42) report random-effect, count, unweighted common-effect, interaction and average-relative-effect analyses, but no severity weights or weighted result.

Table 2 (p. 8, rendered): monitoring 632/982 (64.9) and 651/984 (67.7); reversal 724/982 (74.3) and 723/984 (75.2). 632/982 = 64.4%, 651/984 = 66.2%, 724/982 = 73.7%, 723/984 = 73.5%. The printed percentages equal counts over the neuromuscular-blockade denominators 974/961 (64.9, 67.7, 74.3, 75.2), whereas the differences (-1.8, 0.2) use 982/984.

Table 3 (p. 9): disseminated intravascular coagulation 1 (0.1) vs 0, 'RR 2.00 (1.91 to 2.09)', P > .99. A CI excluding 1 is incompatible with P > .99 (Fisher P = 1.0), and a finite RR with a narrow CI is not estimable from 1 vs 0 events. 2.00 equals the high-PEEP risk over the pooled risk (see C004).

Table 3 (p. 9): in-hospital mortality 12 (1.2) vs 5 (0.5), RR 1.41 (0.95 to 1.81), P = .09. On the log scale the interval is asymmetric (0.395 below vs 0.250 above the estimate) unlike neighboring rows, and it is far too narrow for 17 deaths: crude RR 2.40 (0.85-6.77). The P value matches an uncorrected chi-square test on the counts (.089); the estimate and interval do not.

Protocol Appendix iii (supp1 p. 31): mild respiratory failure = PaO2 <60 mm Hg or SpO2 <90% on room air >=10 min but responding to supplemental O2; moderate = the same despite supplemental O2. eMethods §2.8 (supp4 p. 20) and Table 3 note d: mild = responding to O2 2 L/min; moderate = responding only to O2 >2 L/min. The mild/moderate boundary moves from response vs non-response to an oxygen-flow threshold.

Protocol extrapulmonary definitions (supp1 p. 32, rendered at 400 dpi): coma = Glasgow Coma Score <= 8 (underlined less-than sign; the text layer shows '<'). eMethods §2.8 (supp4 p. 21, rendered): coma = GCS < 8. Only a GCS of exactly 8 is classified differently; 2 vs 2 coma events.

eTable 8 per-protocol (supp4 p. 29, rendered): cardiopulmonary edema 15/917 vs 7/912, 'Effect estimate 1.36 (1.02-1.82)', P = 0.09. The interval excludes 1 while P > .05. Crude RR = 2.13 (0.87-5.20), uncorrected chi-square P = .089, matching the printed P; 1.36 equals the high-PEEP/pooled risk ratio (C004).

Main p1 abstract and p3 Results print the surgery HbA1c change as 1.6% with 95% CI -1.8% to -1.3% (point outside its interval) and the medical change as 0.2% (-0.5% to 0.2%); Table 2 p6 gives signed -1.6 and -0.2 with the same CIs. Mixed sign convention; direction is clear from 'decreased' and Table 2.

Year-12 HbA1c difference -1.1% (-1.7 to -0.5) is given P=.002 in main p1/p3 but P<.001 in eTable 2 (supp 2 p15), same model and interval. Wald P from the CI = .0003 (worst-case rounding .0015); the two printed P values conflict; inference unchanged.

Abstract p1: '4 deaths (2.2%), 2 in each group' with N=262 enrolled; 4/262 = 1.5%. Table 3 p8 arm values 2/96=2.1% and 2/166=1.2% reproduce. No alternative denominator is stated. Counts are correct, so the percentage alone is wrong.

Protocol v6 p17, p26-27, p29 define the primary outcome as relative percent change in HbA1c (power assumes -15% vs -7% to +2%); the report's Table 2 footnote b (p6) and eTable 2 present net (absolute) change in HbA1c units (-1.4 points), while main p2 still calls it 'percent change'.

Protocol p18 and Table A1 p29 define remission as HbA1c <6.5% off diabetes medications with no duration; main p2 requires no medications for at least 3 months, assessed annually. The report adds an operational window; threshold and medication criterion agree.

Protocol Table A1 p30 lists major adverse cardiovascular events under Aim 2 Safety (vascular efficacy outcomes are stroke, retinopathy, nephropathy, foot ulcer); main p2 lists major adverse cardiovascular events among 'other secondary outcomes'. Plan p18 says some study outcomes are also secondary endpoints without naming them.

Planned primary model A1 (protocol p26) adjusts for group, visit, group x visit and site only; baseline HbA1c appears among further sensitivity covariates (p34). The reported primary model (main p2-3; supp 2 p4) includes baseline HbA1c as a fixed effect.

Planned sensitivity analyses (protocol p30-31, p34: MICE with Rubin's rules, pattern-mixture models, MSM with combined treatment and censoring weights, per-protocol discarding post-crossover outcomes, expanded baseline-covariate models) are not reported; the report gives only an IPW per-protocol analysis with treatment weights (main p3; supp 2 p5).

Plan model A2 (protocol p27) is a mixed-effects logistic model with a patient random intercept for glycemic control and remission; the report (main p3; supp 2 p4) analyzes these outcomes with GEE and sandwich SEs, adjusting for baseline HbA1c. No A2 result is reported.

Table 2 p6, medical group change OR for diabetes medication use 0.10 (0.01 to 3.27): geometric CI midpoint 0.18 (rounding range 0.128-0.222), while all 17 other OR cells in the table reproduce sqrt(L*U) within rounding. Point or a limit likely misprinted; within-group change, not the group comparison.

Plan p34 specifies Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel (site-stratified) tests for microvascular/macrovascular and safety outcomes; supp 2 p6 and eTable 5/6 footnotes state chi-squared or Fisher exact tests, with no stratification mentioned.

Within the protocol, model A1 (p26) treats site as fixed (Z site vector and b_i 'fixed effect for site'), but the power section (p28) uses a fitted site variance component sigma_b=0.06 and p31 describes site effects as following a distribution with the CI reflecting heterogeneity. The operative fixed-site specification is clear and matches the report.

Protocol Appendix 2 (p55-56): randomized 155+69+43+45+43=355, underwent intervention 154+61+38+40+32=325 (also p27), implying 30 not treated, but the dagger footnote says 38 dropped at randomization. Background participant accounting; the 302 eligible figure (140+56+35+39+32) is unaffected.

eTable 1 (supp 2 p14), 7-year column N=262: Other race 4 (1.9); 4/262=1.5%. Race counts 81+176+4=261, not 262; main Table 1 gives White 59+118=177 (67.6%) and Other 2+2=4, whereas eTable 1 and the abstract give White 176 (67.2%).

Main p4: follow-up imaging was MRI in 8 of 336 (2%) and CT in 328 (98%); p9 and eTable 11 (supp 5 p51; N 101+24+79=204) describe 204 (61%) patients with MR diffusion follow-up; p11 says 'two-thirds'. The count of the post hoc infarct-growth population is irreconcilable within the report.

Analysis SAP (supp 4 p3, section 5.1) states all analyses will be as-treated; the report (main p4) analyzes treatment-effect comparisons across imaging strata by randomized group and within-group associations as-treated (Figure 1; Figure 2 labeled intention to treat). Two crossovers, so numerical impact likely small.

Analysis SAP p3 makes composite core (larger of CTP/MRI and CT hypodensity) the primary volume and CTP/MRI core a sensitivity analysis; the appendix (p7) calls composite core pre-specified. The report uses CTP/MRI core as the main measure and labels composite-core analyses post hoc (main p4, p6; Figure 3; eFigure 10).

eFigures 7 and 8 (supp 5 p13-14): ASPECTS 0-2 (n=19) has 0 events in both arms for mRS 0-2 and for mRS 0-3, yet both print RR 1.00 (0.37-2.72), identical across outcomes; other zero-cell rows (e.g., >=150 mL) print '*'. A risk ratio is not estimable with no events in either arm.

Figure 2B (main p7, core >=100 mL): segment colors assign EVT 2/6/10/20 to mRS 0-3 (no mRS 4 segment), giving mRS 0-2 18% and 0-3 38%; eFigures 7-8 give 4/51 (7.8%) and 9/51 (17.6%), and the Discussion says about 80% had mRS >=4. The values fit if each segment is shifted one category (mRS 1-6); MM bar shows the same shift.

Main p8 states that as mismatch volume increased the marginal probability of mRS 0-2 and 0-3 increased with EVT and decreased with MM; eFigure 17A/B (supp 5 p23) shows both EVT curves (and MM curves) decreasing across mismatch volume.

E changed: the issue is which core variable conditions the age/time surfaces, a labeling conflict rather than a numerical error. eFigure 18 title says CTP/MRI core while its explanation says composite core; eFigure 19 uses composite core; main p10 cites both and says 'consistent across estimated CT perfusion/MRI core volumes'.

Analysis SAP p5 (section 5.2.3) plans predicted probabilities of independent ambulation by age and time from last known well to randomization in EVT patients; the report shows age by time from CTP to reperfusion/end of procedure (eFigure 18) and from LKW to reperfusion/end of procedure (eFigure 19). No LKW-to-randomization surface is reported.

Protocol (Aug 2021) synopsis p8 and section 3.7.1.1 p37 call mRS 0-2 the second primary outcome, but protocol p50 calls it 'our secondary endpoint'; the trial SAP v1.0.0 (Nov 2022, p13, p17) lists it as secondary. Infarct volume/lesion growth are secondary in protocol p50 but tertiary in SAP p13.

Protocol Appendix B (p80-81) and trial SAP (p39-40): W is the rank sum of mRS scores in the EVT group and efficacy is claimed if Z >= b; H_A is P(Y <= X) = 1/2 + theta with Y = MM and X = EVT mRS. As written, large values indicate worse (higher) EVT mRS, opposite to benefit (lower mRS, p37).

Trial SAP section 7.2 (p9) and Appendix B (p40) prespecify interim looks at 200 and 380 patients; section 7.5 (p12) says the DSMB 300-patient review was provided 'without making any alteration to the study design or incorporating any additional interim analyses', yet the trial was stopped because the efficacy boundary was crossed at 300 using 'pre-specified boundaries'. The boundary applicable at 300 is not specified.

Analysis SAP p5 (5.2.5) defines sICH with a >=4-point NIHSS increase 'at 4-hour follow-up window' and no death component; trial SAP p13 uses '>=4-point increase ... or death within 24 hours' and p18/p31 a 24-hour window. Report cites SITS-MOST and reports counts only.

Analysis SAP p6 (5.3.3) plans stratification by mismatch volume thresholds of 50 and 100 mL; neither the main article nor supplement 5 reports these strata (only the two ratio/volume mismatch profiles and a continuous mismatch-volume analysis, eFigure 17).

eFigure 13 (supp 5 p19), RR of mRS 5-6 (adverse) with EVT vs MM: all 16 RRs are below 1 (favoring EVT), but the axis labels read 'Favours Medical Management' on the left and 'Favours Thrombectomy' on the right. eFigure 9 (p15), the same outcome, labels the axis correctly.

Discordant profile 2 (ASPECTS 6-10, core >=70 mL): eTable 9 MM has mRS 0-3 3/11 and mRS 5-6 10/11 (13 > 11); eTable 10 MM has 4/12 and 11/12 (15 > 12) and mRS 0-2 2/12 with 11/12. eTable 8 attributes the favorable counts to EVT (mRS 0-2 1/12, 0-3 3/12; MM 0/11), so arms appear swapped for favorable outcomes in eTables 9-10.

Protocol (Aug 2021) p48: at the final analysis, if the overall efficacy bound is not crossed, an optimal subgroup is selected and tested; trial SAP v1.0.0 (Nov 2022) p10: if the final efficacy bound is not crossed, EVT is declared not superior (no subgroup rescue). The final stage was never reached (trial stopped at the 300-patient review).

Protocol p5 primary analysis: logistic regression with 'all estimates adjusted for baseline confounders'; report p4 uses ordinary logistic regression with no covariates named, and Table 2 RR 1.35 (1.17-1.57) and OR 1.57 reproduce the crude 287/759 vs 208/744 exactly. The primary estimates appear unadjusted.

Main p2 says the waitlist group was not included in tests of statistical significance; p4 reports retention P=.02 (1 month) and P=.11 (7 months). These reproduce only as 3-group chi-square tests including waitlist (P=.017, .115); the 2-group tests give P=.009 and .073. Conclusions about retention are unchanged.

E changed: main article p3 says participants who set a quit date receive messages 6 weeks before and 8 weeks after it; the results supplement eAppendix A (supp 2 p2) says 1 week before and 8 weeks after, as does the protocol (p2). The plan only corroborates the supplement, so this is a report-internal conflict about the intervention.

Protocol p5-6: identify potential moderators (e.g., age, gender, motivation) and examine treatment-by-moderator interactions for those associated with the primary outcome; report p4-5 and eAppendix D/eTable 6 test every Table 1 characteristic one at a time with Holm adjustment across about 25 tests.

eTable 5 (supp 2 p14), 30-day IPRW OR 1.92 (1.50, 2.24): a log-symmetric interval with lower 1.50 implies an upper limit near 2.46 (1.92^2/1.50); all 11 other RR/OR cells in the table are log-symmetric within rounding. The IPRW interval is also narrower than the CCA OR interval, unlike the RR rows.

Both protocol versions (supp 2 p41 line 759; p103 line 1778) and both SAP versions (p140 line 2357; p160 line 2767) specify BMI subgroups <25, 25-30 and >=30 kg/m2; Figure 2 (main p7) uses <25 vs >=25, while main p4 states all forest-plot subgroups were prespecified.

Table S7 (supp 1 p20) headers say N=233/238 (per-protocol) but its site totals 256+245=501 and events 4+7=11, 19+15=34 are the primary analysis population; Table S8 (p21), titled per-protocol, has headers n=249/252 although its counts reproduce with 233/238 (9/233=3.9%, 33/238=13.9%, 20/238=8.4%). The two tables' headers appear swapped.

Table S6 (supp 1 p19), center-adjusted primary analysis with n=249/252, gives balloon events 9 (3.9) vs 11 (4.4) in Table 2 and Figure 2; 9/249=3.6%, whereas 9/233=3.9% matches the per-protocol count (Table S8). Adjustment does not change event counts; the HR 0.32 (0.16-0.62) matches the main analysis, suggesting a transcription error in the count.

Table 2 (main p8), any stroke outside the qualifying territory within 1 year, 3 (1.2) vs 4 (1.6): incidence difference -0.4 (95% CI -2.4 to -1.7), HR 0.76, P=.72. The point lies outside its interval and the interval excludes 0. Wald recomputation gives -0.38 (-2.44 to 1.67): the upper limit has lost its sign.
Figure S4 (supp 1 p13), balloon group mRS 2 at 90 days: '2.0 (N=50)'; 50/249=20.1%, and with 50 the category counts sum to 294, not 249. N=5 gives 2.0% and a total of 249 (205+36+5+2+0+1+0).

Both SAP versions (p142 lines 2387-2389; p162 lines 2803-2805) specify Fisher exact tests for grouped AEs; Table S11 (supp 1 p24) footnotes label overall, nervous-system and disabling-stroke rows as chi-square. Recomputed, the printed P values (0.84, 0.35, 0.02) match Fisher (0.841, 0.350, 0.020), not Pearson (0.71, 0.25, 0.013) or Yates (0.865, 0.363, 0.023) for the first two, so the difference appears to be in labeling only.

Original protocol synopsis (supp 2 p11-12): 686 patients, 91 endpoint events, '90% confidence', Lan-DeMets; section 20.1 (p40-41): 686 patients, 80% power, O'Brien-Fleming. With 12.76% vs 6.25% one-year risk and 1:1 allocation, 686 patients give about 65 first-year events, and the required events are about 56 (80%) or 75 (90%). The 91-event figure does not reproduce; the design was later re-estimated to 512.

Protocol (supp 1 p11) and SAP (p36) specify that if residuals of the primary model are substantially non-normal, two sensitivity analyses will be done: a normalizing transformation and an ordinal regression. eFigure 1 (supp 2 p18) reports residuals 'clearly non-normal' and gives only the square-root transformation; no ordinal model of the total score is reported in the main article or supplement 2.

Protocol p11-12 and SAP p34-37 plan between-group models for individual SSPedi symptoms and for symptom documentation and interventions at weeks 4 and 8. The report gives week-8 comparisons only; week 4 appears descriptively (eTable 9, supp 2 p12) without comparative estimates.

Final protocol item 5 (supp 1 p12) and SAP (p37): intervention outcomes analyzed as simple differences in proportions ignoring clustering, Fisher exact P values and Newcombe CIs. Report (main p4; eTable 10 footnote b; eMethods p22) presents odds ratios from mixed or fixed effects logistic regression for any and symptom-specific interventions.

eTable 10 (supp 2 p13-14), mouth sores among SSPedi>=3: symptom screening 0/0 (empty), yet finite ORs are printed: 2.6 (0.04-170.4), 5.00 (0.07-366.4) twice. These equal Haldane 0.5-corrected crude ORs ((0.5x6.5)/(0.5x2.5)=2.6; (0.5x7.5)/(0.5x1.5)=5.0), a method not described; a comparison with an empty group is not estimable.

eTable 10 symptom-specific intervention, SSPedi>=1: neuropathy 6/57 vs 0/70, OR 17.8 (0.98-323.1), P=.007; hunger 6/111 vs 0/130, OR 16.08 (0.9-288.74), P=.009; main p6 calls both significant. Recomputed: the ORs/CIs are Haldane-corrected Wald values and the P values are Fisher exact (.0070, .0089), not the logistic models the footnote states. CI and P come from different, undisclosed methods.

Abstract (main p1): 'Among the 338 randomized infants ..., 320 underwent operative repair'. Figure 1 (p3) and text (p4-5) give 152 early (147+5) and 129 late (90+39) repairs = 281; 320 is the number remaining after withdrawals (163+157), the population described in Table 1.

Protocol v7 p13: primary outcome by binomial GLMM with log link; hospital days by a lognormal model. SAP (Oct 2022) p7-8: logistic model for binary outcomes and negative binomial for counts, same model for frequentist and Bayesian analyses. Report p4: logistic mixed model (Bayesian), but frequentist primary by GEE logistic due to nonconvergence (disclosed), and negative binomial mixed model for hospital days.

SAP p8: prior for categorical outcomes OR 1.0 with 95% CrI 0.2-4 (Normal(0, 0.7) on log OR); count outcomes RR 95% CrI 0.33-3.3; interaction terms Normal(0, 0.6); subgroup main effects as primary. Protocol p13: RR 1.0 (0.33-3.0) and main effects N(0,1000). Report p4: OR/RR 1.0 (95% CrI 0.33-3.0) for the intervention effect and 0.33-3.0 for interactions, vague priors for other terms.

Protocol v7 (p14, p25) and SAP p4: one formal interim analysis (efficacy threshold 95%) when 10-month data were available for about 200 infants, planned for December 2019. Report p4: formal interim analysis completed with data for 309 infants in February 2021, which crossed the 95% threshold and stopped enrollment.

SAP (p4-5, p8-9) plans: per-protocol analysis of the primary outcome, probabilities of at least 3% and 5% risk reduction, Bayesian/frequentist analysis of death as an important secondary outcome, modifiers maternal education, prenatal care, difficult-to-reduce hernia (and sex, race/ethnicity), and continuous GA modeling. None is reported in the main article or supplement 3; the report shows GA, BPD and open/laparoscopic subgroups only.

Protocol p3 specific aim states expected median hospital days 18 (early) vs 15 (late); protocol p12 power section uses median 8 vs 5 (means 18 vs 13). The SAP (p3, lines 76-79) explicitly identifies the p3 values as incorrect and confirms 8 vs 5.

Abstract (p1) and Results (p5) state no significant difference in any of the 11 secondary end points, but Table 2 (p6) gives EQ-5D-5L postoperative day 5 difference -0.057 (95% CI -0.111 to -0.003), P=.04, favoring placebo. The SAP (p14) specifies no multiplicity adjustment and time-point effects from the time-by-treatment model.

SAP p13: safety data presented for participants randomized who received the IMP. Figure 1 (main p3) labels 279 lidocaine (including 12 who did not receive treatment) and 279 placebo (including 13 non-recipients plus 1 excluded participant who received drug) as the safety analysis; Table 3 (p8) headers are 279/278.

Protocol (supp 1 endpoint definitions and concomitant-medication section) and SAP data schedule (p10-11): total postoperative opioid consumption cumulative to 72 hours after start of operation. Report (p4-6, Table 2): postoperative opioid consumption up to 24 hours.

Methods (main p4) list total length of hospital stay among 5 tertiary objectives and Table 3 is titled Tertiary/Safety Outcomes, but the Discussion (p7) says the trial showed no benefit on 'any of the 11 secondary end points including ... total length of hospital stay'. Protocol and SAP also classify it as tertiary.
Protocol and SAP (p10, p27 Table 13.23): unplanned readmissions within 30 days of the date of operation. Report Table 3 (p8): unplanned readmission after discharge and within 90 days of operation.

Protocol section 10.2 (supp 1 PDF p40): primary outcome analyzed with a GLM with logit link. SAP v2 (p14, Table 13.8, Stata code p34): log link (Poisson, robust). Report (p5-6): log-link GLM, relative risk 0.97 (0.88-1.07).

SAP shell Tables 13.8-13.10 and 13.21-13.22 (p20-21, p26) plan unadjusted and adjusted estimates for the primary outcome (ITT and per-protocol), GI-2/GI-3 times, prolonged ileus and discharge readiness; only adjusted estimates are reported (Table 2). L left blank: a real omission but of low importance in a randomized trial.
SAP section 11.6 (p15): sensitivity analysis comparing Edinburgh (sponsor, largest recruiter) with the other centres. Not reported in the main article or supplements 3-4.

SAP shell Tables 13.21-13.22 (p26) and Stata code (p36) specify a generalized linear model (meglm, continuous time) for time to medical discharge criteria and to patient-reported readiness; the report (p5, p7 Table 2) uses Cox regression (HR 0.99 for both). The SAP's general text (p14, 11.4) says time-to-event outcomes use Cox regression.

SAP shell tables plan outputs not found in the report: GI-2 status by 96 h (Table 13.7), total vomiting episodes and rescue antiemetic dose to 72 h, EQ-5D VAS at postoperative time points, and day-1 weight (ERAS table). Report gives other components of these outcome families. L left blank: descriptive components of low importance.

Protocol endpoint definitions (supp 1 p16) and SAP prose (p9, p33) time GI-2/GI-3 recovery from surgery/start of operation; the SAP variable definitions for the Cox models (p34) use the start of general anaesthesia as time origin.

SAP 11.5 (p14-15) says subgroup interactions are added to the primary model (age group, sex, centre), but the ERAS-adherence sample command (p38) omits AgeBand while the other subgroup commands include it.

Subgroup eFigure (supp 3 p2): legend labels the horizontal lines '99% CI', while the caption says the numbers are 95% CIs. The plotted lines coincide with the printed numeric limits (e.g., overall 0.88-1.07; low ERAS 0.49-2.08), and the overall row equals the main 95% CI. SAP p15 specifies 99% CIs for subgroups.

Abstract (p1): patients were 'randomly assigned ... restrictive (n = 733) or liberal (n = 724)' and '1979 randomized, 1508 completed the trial'. Figure 1 (p3): 983 restrictive and 994 liberal randomized (plus 2 lost envelopes = 1979); 750/758 remained after post-randomization exclusions; 17 and 34 then withdrew or were lost, leaving 733/724 analyzed. Protocol (supp 1 p13, p26, p49, p62): inclusion continues up to a maximum of 1600 participants and ends at 1420 evaluable participants with 30-day follow-up; SAP (p85) and report (p5): 1420 total including 3.5% dropout. Report: 1979 randomized, 1508 after secondary exclusions, 1457 analyzed.

Protocol (p13, p23, p49, p59) lists 9 secondary outcomes without hierarchy; the SAP (Jan 2023, p85-89) and report (p5-6) designate death and major respiratory complications as 2 key secondary outcomes and the rest as exploratory with Benjamini-Hochberg control. Report follows the SAP.

SAP (p88) and report (p5): adjusted for stratification variables (site of inclusion, intubation), with an additional model adding age, sex, ISS and GCS; no model includes pneumonia on admission.

Protocol (p26, p62) and SAP (p89) list a primary-outcome subgroup for episodes of hypoxemia during the intervention (SpO2 <90%); Figure 4 (main p8) and eTable 7 (supp 2 p20-21) report six subgroups without it.

Protocol (p26, p62) and SAP (p89) define the intubation subgroup as initially intubated within 1 hour of the accident/trauma; Figure 4 and eTable 7 use 'intubated at randomization' (the stratification variable).

Protocol (p26, p62): secondary outcomes compared by Fisher exact/chi-square tests for categorical data. SAP (p89) and report (p5-6, Figure 2): key secondary outcomes (death, major respiratory complications) analyzed with logistic regression (GEE, IPW) as ORs.

SAP Table (supp 1 p101): SSI = purulent drainage; positive microbiology from the site AND signs of infection; or surgeon diagnosis. Results supplement eMethods (supp 2 p9): purulent drainage; positive microbiology (no signs required); deliberately opened by a surgeon AND signs; or surgeon diagnosis.

Also in the same table, restrictive firearm injury has denominator 724 (8/724) where all other mechanism rows use 742.

Disclosed in the report (p4) with a rationale; no plan provision supplied.

Their weight and probability basis are not stated.

Varenicline nonabstainers: switch to CNRT 0/41 (0%) vs continue 2/77 (3%). Discussion (p8) correctly describes a decrement with switching.

Protocol p28 and p30: analyses with and without potential confounders, joint modeling of outcomes and missingness, pattern-mixture models for non-ignorable missingness, and sensitivity analyses with optimistic/pessimistic/skeptical priors. None is reported in the main article or supplement 2; only a post hoc dynamic treatment regime analysis is added.

EOT+30 continuous abstinence, varenicline nonabstainers who continued: main p7 and supp 2 p10 give n = 42; eFigure 2 (supp 2 p15) gives 0/77, the continuation group used in all analyses (42 re-randomized + 35 assigned).

The CNRT figures conflate an RD with an arm rate and misstate continuation as 0%.

Protocol Figure 2 (supp 1 p32), repeated in eFigure 1 (supp 2 p14): week-6 response '0.48, 0.38-0.58 ~Beta(193,210)' and '0.50, 0.40-0.60 ~Beta(785,869)'. These betas give 95% intervals 0.43-0.53 and 0.45-0.50 (mean 0.475 for the second), whereas the 8 week-12 boxes reproduce their stated intervals.

That interval corresponds to SD = 10 (variance 100); variance 10 (SD 3.16) gives 0.0020 to 492. The main text (p4) also writes the coefficient prior as N(mu=0, sigma=1000), i.e., SD notation.

Main p.3 says plasma NfL was prespecified (regimen-only samples); Supp3 p.6 and p.11 say plasma NfL was added post hoc (PD SAP originally specified UCH-L1 only). Main p.4 says '4 of the 41 participants in the regimen placebo group and 2 in the shared placebo group were excluded' for no follow-up time, but Table 2 (p.7) uses 4/41 as regimen-placebo events and only 2 shared-placebo exclusions (164-2=162). Printed P values reproduce almost exactly if each interval is estimate +/- 1 SE (r = 0.999 over rows with P>=.001; SE implied by P is 1.95 x the 95%-CI SE), so the 'CIs' are ~68% intervals. Not found in any report document (main article; Supp3 index of 9 eTables and 7 eFigures; Supp4 is the investigator list): SAP §7 center and treatment-by-center interaction model, SAP §7.2 seven prespecified subgroup interactions with forest plot (ICEMAN addendum pp.14-15), protocol §11.4.3(b) treatment x stroke type and (c) added-covariable analyses. No stated reason (e.g., PO assumption failure).

SAP §9.4.1-9.4.2 and §7.7 (Supp3 pp.29, 38; OCR) plan primary-outcome replication in the SAF (as-treated) population, a baseline-covariate-adjusted model, and treatment interactions with site, GA stratum, race and sex for the primary (BPD/death) outcome. Protocol synopsis and §3.2 (Supp1 pp.6, 15; OCR) define the primary end point as >=5% weight loss OR >=4% loss + >=150 min/wk PA OR >=0.2-point HbA1c reduction; the report (main pp.1, 3-4) additionally requires HbA1c <6.5% throughout. Protocol §9.3 (Supp1 p.37; OCR) excludes participants who withdraw from effectiveness analyses; report analyzes all 368 randomized and counts missing 12-month visits (26 AI, 29 human) as failures (main p.4; Figure 1). Disclosed in the SAP change table (Supp1 p.86).

Protocol §9.4.7-9.4.8 (Supp1 p.38; OCR) analyzes the primary and component end points with (mixed-effects) logistic regression; report uses unadjusted binomial regression for the risk difference (main p.4). Disclosed in the SAP change table (Supp1 p.86); cluster-robust SEs added post hoc (eTables 19a-b).

Main p.3 says the primary analysis was adjusted on the minimization stratification factors, which p.2 defines as etiology and center; Table 2 footnote c (p.6) says the Fine-Gray model was adjusted for etiology only, as does the SAP §3.5 (Supp2 p.6, OCR). Protocol (Supp1 pp.14-15 and repeats) and SAP §2.2/§3.6 (Supp2 pp.4, 7-8) plan ECMO-free and ventilation-free days at D30 and D60; main p.3 lists both windows as predefined, but only day-30 values are reported (Table 2 p.6; eTable 3 Supp3 p.5). Report (main p.3): quit date set 5 days after enrollment, and continuous abstinence is counted from it. Plan (protocol pp.8, 47; SAP p.84; OCR): cotinine by Accutest NicAlert strips, level <3 (100-200 ng/mL) = abstinent. Report (main p.3): a rapid test cassette (AllTest) with 'a negative result' = abstinent; no cutoff given. Device differs and the equivalence of thresholds cannot be checked.

Protocol v6.0 §28.2.2 (Supp1 p.66; v4.0 p.28; OCR) plans GLMMs with log link and Poisson distribution to estimate RRs; the report (main p.3) uses mixed-effects logistic regression, as does the SAP (p.91-92). Report follows the SAP, not the protocol.

Methods (main p.3) describe mixed-effects logistic models but Table 2 reports RRs with no conversion stated. The headline 'crude' RR 3.0 (2.0-4.9) differs from the crude ratio 300/720 vs 55/360 = 2.73 and from eTable 8 'All' unadjusted RR 2.890 (1.983-4.709) for the same ITT outcome.

SAP §'Adjusted analyses' (Supp1 p.92, OCR) plans a fully adjusted model including tobacco use form with education, smoking duration and other baseline characteristics; the report's adjusted RR 3.2 (2.2-5.2) uses covariates 'selected post hoc' (age, sex, education, occupation, smoking duration), without tobacco form (main pp.3-4, Table 2 note a). Disclosed as post hoc.

Planned primary outcome uses CO <10 ppm (SAP p.84); the CO <6 ppm analysis is described as post hoc sensitivity (main p.3) but its ITT and PP rows sit under the 'Primary outcome' heading of Table 2 (p.6). Labeling issue; the text makes the status clear.

Protocol v6.0/v4.0 §28.2.2/§11.2.2 (Supp1 pp.66, 28; OCR) plan primary analysis 'in a missing-at-random architecture'; the SAP (p.91) and report (main p.3) treat missing primary outcomes as not abstinent (Russell Standard), with complete-case analysis as sensitivity.

SAP subgroup analyses (Supp1 pp.92-93, OCR) include gender (male vs female); the report's prespecified subgroup list (main p.3) and eTable 8 (Supp2 p.12) omit sex and add an ability-to-read-SMS subgroup. No reason given (only 37 women enrolled).

Changed from protocol_report. SAP v2.0 (18 May 2024, after last follow-up 29 Apr 2024; pp.63, 66-67) and the report (main pp.3, 5-6) use a responder end point (>=1.4-point decrease), Fisher exact test, and deaths imputed as SOFA 24.

SAP (Supp1 p.66; OCR) and Methods (main p.5) carry the last SOFA forward for patients discharged home before day 9; but SOFA was captured only during ICU stay (p.3) and Results (p.6) state 8.3% had SOFA carried forward because of ICU discharge before day 9 (eTable 8). Implemented rule = ICU discharge.

Report (main pp.5, 7; Table 2 note b): reversal by day 28, persistence over later draws and >=2 serial draws required, no ferritin condition for immunoparalysis, analyzed in a 125-patient subset.

Protocol v1.0 (Supp1 p.26; OCR) powers the trial for a 1.4-point difference in mean SOFA (SD 3.2), two-sided t test, 90% power; the report (main p.5) powers for responder proportions 40% vs 20% (117/group, 280 with 15% dropout). SAP v2.0 has no power section.

Protocol (Supp1 p.27) and SAP (p.70; OCR) compare infection resolution (resolved vs not) by Fisher exact test with MH OR; the report uses ordinal regression over 4 categories (resolved, intermediate, failure, superinfection), OR 0.59 (0.38-0.91) (main p.6-7, Table 2), while stating all analyses followed the SAP.

SAP (Supp1 pp.67-72; OCR) plans Breslow-Day/Tarone comparisons of ORs between immune states and severity strata, survivor-only mean SOFA t tests within strata, mortality by immune state, infection resolution by infection type/stratum, and subgroups by appropriate vs inappropriate antibiotics. None appears in the main article or Supp2 (searched); severity subgroups are reported as 'interaction tests' and called post hoc (main p.5) although the SAP prespecifies them.

Disclosed (SAP change table).

Original and final protocol §4.2.2 (Supp1 pp.30, 70; rendered) plan the primary outcome analysis both adjusted only for the stratification variables (site, HIE, acute brain injury, sepsis) and fully adjusted. Final protocol v1.8 (14 Oct 2024; Supp1 pp.70-71, rendered) analyzes ICU and hospital stay by Wilcoxon rank-sum tests stratified by survival status; the original and final SAPs (pp.104, 128; OCR) and the report (main p.3, Table 2) use Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards among survivors with death as a competing risk. Report follows the SAP.
